t: You're standing in St Alphage Garden, which now occupies the site of St Alphege London Wall, a church built directly upon the old city wall. It was also called St Alphege Cripplegate, after the nearby gate. Only ruins remain. Sir Rowland Hayward is buried here. He was a wealthy London merchant and Lord Mayor in 1570 and again in 1591, and he lent money to Queen Elizabeth the First and entertained her in 1587. Susannah Millner, who passed messages among the Quakers, lived at the sign of the Red Lion on Wood Street.
